verified.note: Everything here is taken from Cursor's current documentation (2026-11-02) and checked by QAMind's conformance suite against that documentation. QAMind has never run inside a real Cursor (neither the editor nor the agent CLI), which is why the tier is experimental.

skills.naming: the folder name is the skill name and the slash command (/qamind-qa-only); the front matter name must equal it
facts: documented front matter: name, description, paths, disable-model-invocation (user-only); user-invocable: false (model-only) appears only in the CLI changelog
allowed-tools, argument-hint and $ARGUMENTS are not documented, so arguments are the text typed after the slash name in the same message
Cursor also reads .claude/skills and .codex/skills; with its Third-Party Imports setting on, a project that has both the Claude plugin and this install may show a skill twice

mcp.registration: ~/.cursor/mcp.json (user) or <project>/.cursor/mcp.json (project), top-level mcpServers; command, args, env, type
facts: the working directory of a stdio server and the meaning of ${workspaceFolder} in the user-level file are not documented: QAMind passes the project folder as QAMIND_PROJECT_DIR and ignores a value that was left unexpanded
the name the model sees for a tool is not documented, so the skills name tools by their short names and the server
Cursor asks for approval of MCP tool calls unless they are on its allowlist (~/.cursor/permissions.json mcpAllowlist, entries server:tool)

hooks.enforcement: auto-QA only. The safety guard is NOT a hook on this host: permission hooks (preToolUse, beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, beforeReadFile) block the action when their output is invalid, and their payloads are only partly documented, so a mistake could stop all of the user's tool use. The safety rules are instructions here.
facts: stop: stdin has conversation_id, status (completed, aborted, error), loop_count and workspace_roots; printing {"followup_message": "..."} submits it as the next user message
loop_count counts the follow-ups already triggered (starts at 0); the default limit is 5 and loop_limit in hooks.json changes it
beforeSubmitPrompt: stdin has prompt, conversation_id and workspace_roots
a hook that crashes or times out lets the action go on unless failClosed is set; project hooks run only in a trusted workspace
the hook process gets CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (an alias for compatibility); user-level hooks run from ~/.cursor, so the project folder comes from that variable

auto_qa.invoke: To run QA, use the skill `qamind-qa-auto-run` (it is in your skills list) with the mode `{mode}`.
